name: dark-mc-plan-r4
context:
A PLAN FOR GAME THREE, SUBMITTED BEFORE ANY CODE IS WRITTEN. Same six-stage structure that game two's Monte Carlo plan was approved under, re-pointed at a procedurally generated universe rather than a board. Nothing here has been built.

─────────── WHAT GAME THREE IS, AND WHY IT IS NOT GAME TWO ───────────

The user's framing: a non-conventional grid -- 3D or even 4D, breaking from the 2D board -- pure Monte Carlo engineered, vertex-GPU rendered, with rounds procedurally generated from a deterministic seed and FULLY REBUILT each game, so every run is new while staying fair, balanced and exploit-free. A seeded universe the player interacts with. A physics sandbox.

The three games must ask three different questions:

    Farkle     "again?"                      risk, discrete, push-your-luck
    Chemical   "what do I make from these?"  construction, conservation-bounded
    Darkmatter "what did I set in motion?"   INTERVENTION IN A RUNNING SYSTEM

That third verb is the one neither other game has. Farkle and Chemical are both TURN-TAKING games on a static substrate: nothing happens unless the player acts. Darkmatter's substrate RUNS. The player perturbs it and the consequence arrives later, through dynamics they did not author. That is the distinguishing mechanic and every stage below is about making it fair rather than chaotic.

─────────── THE RISK THAT IS SPECIFIC TO THIS GAME ───────────

A board can always be dealt fairly; a simulated universe cannot. Three failure modes exist here that do not exist for games one and two:

  1. UNWINNABLE SEEDS. A procedural generator can emit a universe in which no
     strategy reaches any score. Chemical's board generator already refuses a
     dead board -- `drawReactiveBoard` raises rather than serving one -- and the
     same discipline is required here, but the check is far harder because
     viability is a property of the DYNAMICS, not of the initial state.
  2. CHAOTIC DIVERGENCE. If the system is sensitive to initial conditions, two
     nearly identical interventions produce wildly different outcomes, and the
     player learns nothing because nothing is learnable. This is not a
     difficulty problem; it is a FAIRNESS problem, and it is measurable as a
     Lyapunov exponent.
  3. FLOAT DRIFT. The determinism requirement and the physics requirement are in
     direct tension. Floating-point accumulation over thousands of integration
     steps diverges between machines, and the repository's standing rule is no
     floats in engine or settlement code -- Fx Q16.16 only.

─────────── THE FACTORS ───────────

    G1  DIMENSION      3D volume | 4D slice projected to 3
    G2  INTEGRATOR     semi-implicit Euler | velocity Verlet | leapfrog
    G3  TIMESTEP       coarse | fine  (fidelity against determinism budget)
    G4  BODIES         sparse | dense (how much system there is to perturb)
    G5  VERB           impulse | mass injection | field placement | orbit capture
    G6  HORIZON        how many steps run between interventions
    G7  OBSERVABILITY  full state | a forecast cone | IR/UV spectral readout
    G8  OBJECTIVE      capture | stabilise | harvest | survive

─────────── THE STAGES, WHICH DO NOT CHANGE ───────────

STAGE 0 - INSTRUMENT VALIDATION, plus three controls this game needs and game two did not:

  N1 DETERMINISM UNDER REPLAY. The same seed and the same intervention list must
     produce a bitwise-identical final state, on the same machine and across a
     restart. Fx Q16.16 fixed point throughout the integrator, because this check
     cannot pass with floats and the repository already forbids them here.
  N2 THE VIABILITY ORACLE, AND ITS REJECTION RATE AS A GATE. Every seeded
     universe must admit at least one strategy reaching a declared floor score,
     checked before the seed is ever served. The round-one audit of game two's
     plan named the cost precisely: "By filtering for solvability, you are no
     longer testing the procedural generator; you are testing the curator... you
     may conclude the game is balanced and deep, while in reality the generator
     is producing 90% unplayable garbage that the oracle is simply hiding."
     So the rejection rate is REPORTED AND GATED, not hidden: above 20% the
     generator is declared defective and fixed rather than filtered. The audit
     also noted the other end -- a 0% rejection rate suggests a generator
     "only producing the center of the distribution and avoiding the interesting,
     high-variance edges". A healthy generator rejects a few percent.
  N3 LYAPUNOV BOUND. Perturb one intervention by the smallest representable
     amount and measure divergence over the horizon. If the exponent is positive
     and large, outcomes are not attributable to decisions and the game is
     unfair no matter how it scores. This is the control that decides whether a
     physics sandbox can be a fair game at all, and it must be run BEFORE any
     design question, because a negative answer changes the whole design.

STAGE 1 - SCREENING, resolution V. Eight factors again, so the same 2^(8-2) design, 64 cells. Not a fold-over: game two's plan claimed a fold-over would raise resolution IV to V and THE DESIGN'S OWN SELF-CHECK DISPROVED IT -- a fold-over reverses every sign, so an even-length defining word is unchanged by it, and resolution stayed at 4. That correction carries forward here rather than being rediscovered.

STAGE 2 - FULL FACTORIAL on the surviving factors.
STAGE 3 - CONFIRMATION on disjoint seeds.
STAGE 4 - EXPLOIT SWEEP. Game three's exploit surface is larger than game two's and different in kind: energy injection loops, resonance pumping, integrator instability farmed as a score source, and boundary escape. A physics sandbox invites exactly the abuse a board does not, because the player is acting on a system with conserved quantities they may be able to manufacture.
STAGE 5 - POPULATION AND DUAL CONSTRAINT, on the same 15 personas, so all three games are comparable on one population.

─────────── PRE-REGISTERED ACCEPTANCE ───────────

    AGENCY FLOOR      >= 25%    play above the readable rule
    SIGNAL UTILITY    >= 50%    the readout is worth reading
    SEED SHARE        <= 35%    the universe does not decide the game
    LYAPUNOV          bounded   two near-identical plays stay near-identical
    REJECTION RATE    1% - 20%  the generator is neither defective nor timid
    REPLAY DIVERGENCE 0         bitwise, or the game cannot be verified at all
    DOMINATED         false

─────────── THE RENDERING, WHICH IS A SEPARATE CLAIM ───────────

Vertex-GPU rendering of a 3D or 4D structure is a presentation decision and must not be allowed to become a gameplay claim. The repository already has a WebGL2 fallback renderer and a pseudo-3D GL board, and a measured frame budget discipline: frame COST inside the callback plus drops at >= 1.75 refresh periods, never rAF interval, which is vsync-locked and measures the display rather than the renderer. The same discipline applies, and the renderer is gated separately from the design: A GAME THAT IS ONLY GOOD BECAUSE IT LOOKS GOOD HAS NOT PASSED.

On 4D specifically: the user's own framing sets the constraint -- "if it's not too abstract and a human can easily understand the concepts". So 4D is a FACTOR with a comprehension gate, not a premise. If the 4D level cannot be explained in one sentence a player acts on correctly, it loses to 3D regardless of its measured depth.

═══════════ REVISIONS AFTER THE ROUND-ONE REVISE ═══════════

Round one returned REVISE and named the primary technical debt as a three-way war between Determinism, Stability and Scale, plus four findings that change stages rather than wording. All six revisions below are adopted.

REVISION 1 - THE THREE-WAY WAR IS RESOLVED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY CHOOSING A SIDE.

The finding: "If you use a semi-implicit Euler to save on fixed-point complexity, your energy conservation will be terrible, leading to explosive orbits that trigger your N2 Rejection Gate. You are fighting a three-way war between Determinism, Stability, and Scale." And on scale: "Q16.16 provides fixed precision of 1/65536 but limits your integer range to +/-32767... you need the distance between two stars and the gravitational influence of a small mass simultaneously. In fixed-point, you cannot have both."

Both correct, and the second is the one that would have been discovered late. Three changes:

  (a) THE INTEGRATOR FACTOR LOSES ITS UNSTABLE LEVEL BEFORE SCREENING, NOT
      AFTER. Semi-implicit Euler is not symplectic for this problem and its
      energy drift is a known quantity rather than something to discover in a
      32-cell sweep. G2 becomes velocity Verlet against leapfrog, both
      symplectic, and a new stage 0 control DISQUALIFIES any integrator whose
      energy drift exceeds 1% over the full horizon. An integrator that fails
      that control never reaches stage 1. Screening a dial whose low level
      explodes would spend half the design measuring an artefact.

  (b) FIXED POINT GOES TO Q32.32 ON POSITION, KEPT AT Q16.16 ON VELOCITY AND
      FORCE. 64-bit position via a hi/lo integer pair gives the dynamic range
      the audit says Q16.16 cannot: roughly nine decimal digits of integer
      range with 1/4e9 resolution. Determinism is unaffected because integer
      arithmetic is exact at any width; only the cost changes.

  (c) A SOFTENED POTENTIAL, WHICH IS STANDARD N-BODY PRACTICE AND NOT A FUDGE.
      Force goes as 1/(r^2 + eps^2) rather than 1/r^2. Without softening, two
      bodies approaching closely produce an unbounded force, which in fixed
      point is an OVERFLOW rather than a large number -- a wrong answer that
      looks like a number. eps is a declared simulation constant and a new
      stage 0 control N5 RANGE SAFETY asserts that no state variable
      approaches the representable bound over the horizon, on every seed the
      viability oracle accepts.

REVISION 2 - REJECTION RATE IS DEMOTED; SOLUTION-SPACE VARIANCE REPLACES IT AS
THE GENERATOR'S HEALTH METRIC.

The finding: "rejection rate measures solvability, not diversity. A generator could be healthy by your metric while producing 100% of its seeds within a narrow, boring band of stability... A better measure of health is the variance of the solution space across the accepted seeds."

Upheld, and it is a better metric than the one it replaces because it cannot be satisfied by a timid generator. Two responses now gate the generator:

    DIVERSITY    the variance of the CEILING score across accepted seeds, and
                 the number of distinct winning strategy classes. A generator
                 whose accepted universes all reward the same intervention is
                 producing one universe with different textures.
    REJECTION    retained, demoted to a DEFECT DETECTOR only: above 20% the
                 generator is broken. It is no longer evidence of health.

The audit's second half is also taken: seeds the oracle rejects are LOGGED AND CHARACTERISED, so what the curator removed is visible. A rejected class that turns out to be "high-tension survival scenarios" is a design finding, not garbage, and the current oracle would have thrown it away silently.

REVISION 3 - A BLIND-READOUT CONTROL, WHICH IS THE HUMAN TEST DONE
DETERMINISTICALLY.

The finding on what I am most likely wrong about: "G7 Observability... you may find that players are playing blind, making interventions based on intuition rather than the data you provide. You will find this out via Blind Pilot testing: give a tester the raw data, no graphics, and ask them to predict the state after X steps."

The instinct is right and the method does not need a human, which matters because the whole point of the deterministic-agent approach is to avoid needing real user testing to find this class of defect. Stage 0 gains:

    N6 READOUT INFORMATION. Run the SAME agent twice: once with full state,
       once with ONLY what the readout exposes. If the readout-limited agent
       scores at the blind agent's level, the readout carries nothing. If it
       scores at the full-state agent's level, the readout is the full state
       and the game has no hidden information at all. The readout must sit
       strictly between, and that is a measurement rather than a design
       opinion.

This is the same shape as game two's SIGNAL UTILITY gate, which is what makes the three games comparable on one instrument.

REVISION 4 - THE SCREENSAVER DETECTOR.

The finding on how this becomes a tech demo: "The Spectacle of Emergence. If the Objective is too loosely coupled to the Intervention, the player will spend the entire game watching beautiful procedurally generated collisions that they did not cause and cannot control... you have built a screensaver, not a game."

That is testable with one more agent and it is cheap:

    N7 DO-NOTHING BASELINE. An agent that never intervenes. If it scores near
       the readable rule, the universe is producing the score and the player is
       an observer. ATTRIBUTION -- the share of final-score variance explained
       by interventions rather than by the seed -- is gated at the same 35% seed
       share the other two games use.

A do-nothing agent is also the correct floor for this game, where game two's floor was a random legal move. Random and do-nothing are the same thing on a static board and very different things on a running one.

REVISION 5 - MOMENTUM IS A REQUIREMENT WITH A NUMBER ON IT.

The finding on whether the third verb is real: "To be a true third verb, the system must possess momentum -- the state must evolve according to its own internal logic during the intervals of player inactivity... If the player's intervention is a perturbation of a trajectory rather than a placement on a grid, the verb is distinct."

So it stops being a claim and becomes a control. Under the DO-NOTHING agent, state change per horizon must be non-trivial and bounded: a system that does not move between interventions is a board game with a wait animation, and one that moves unboundedly is the chaos N3 already rejects. Both ends are failures and both are now measured.

REVISION 6 - ORDER OF OPERATIONS, BECAUSE N3 CAN END THE PROJECT.

N3's Lyapunov bound is promoted to the FIRST thing run, before the generator, the oracle or any factor. The audit's reasoning is why: "A sandbox is for exploration; a game is for mastery. Mastery requires that the player's agency produces a discernible, repeatable signal. If lambda is too high, the signal-to-noise ratio of human intent drops to zero."

If the dynamics are chaotic at the horizon the design needs, no amount of factor screening rescues it and the honest move is to change the physics -- shorter horizons, heavier damping, fewer bodies -- or to abandon the premise. Spending the screening budget first and discovering it afterward is the expensive order.

═══════════ REVISIONS AFTER THE ROUND-TWO REVISE ═══════════

Round two returned REVISE with one finding that no control in the plan covered, and three refinements. The headline: "the distinction between a PHYSICS exploit and a MATH exploit."

REVISION 7 - THE MATH EXPLOIT, WHICH N1 THROUGH N7 WOULD ALL HAVE PASSED.

The finding: "Numerical Resonance (Quantization Exploits). N1-N7 check the game's fairness, but they do not check if the fixed-point arithmetic itself creates non-physical attractors. An agent may find a glitch where rounding errors in the Q32.32/Q16.16 interaction create a localized, non-physical energy gain."

This is the most valuable thing either audit has produced, because every control in the plan would have reported a healthy game. Determinism (N1) PASSES -- a rounding exploit is perfectly deterministic and replays bitwise. Viability (N2) passes. Lyapunov (N3) passes, and in fact a rounding attractor is the opposite of chaotic. Range safety (N5) passes because the gain is localised. The readout (N6) and attribution (N7) both pass, because the player really is causing the score. A deterministic, replayable, attributable, well-conditioned way to manufacture energy from arithmetic is exactly what those seven checks are shaped to approve.

Three changes, and the first is a cause rather than a detector:

  (a) ROUND-TO-NEAREST-EVEN, NOT TRUNCATION, ON EVERY FIXED-POINT MULTIPLY.
      Truncation biases every product toward zero, so the error is not noise, it
      has a SIGN -- and a systematic sign is precisely what integrates into a
      directional drift over thousands of steps. Round-to-nearest-even makes the
      rounding error zero-mean, which turns a drift into a random walk. This is
      the difference between an arithmetic that leaks and one that jitters.

  (b) N8 QUANTISATION CONSERVATION. Run closed systems with NO intervention for
      many horizons and test the conserved quantities for DIRECTIONAL drift
      rather than for magnitude. A bounded random walk in total energy is the
      expected cost of fixed point and is acceptable. A monotone trend is an
      exploit source whether or not anyone has found it yet, and it fails.
      Testing magnitude alone would pass a slow leak, which is the dangerous
      case because a slow leak is exactly what an agent farms.

  (c) AN ADVERSARIAL AGENT WHOSE OBJECTIVE IS THE ARITHMETIC, NOT THE SCORE.
      Stage 4 gains a GLITCH-HUNTER that optimises for total system energy
      rather than for points. If it finds unbounded gain, the integrator is
      broken and the game is unshippable regardless of how it scores. This is
      the deterministic equivalent of turning a speedrunner loose on it, and it
      belongs in the exploit sweep rather than in the balance stages.

REVISION 8 - N6 IS GATED ON THE MEDIAN PERSONA, NOT ON AN IDEAL READER.

The finding: "'Strictly between' is a necessary but insufficient condition. It ensures the readout contains information, but it does not ensure that information is cognitively accessible to a human. N6 must be validated against the specific cognitive profiles of the 15 personas."

Correct, and my version had a hole the persona population already fills. A readout that only the highest searchDepth persona can exploit is technically informative and practically unreadable, and averaging over the population would hide that behind the strong readers. So N6 runs the readout-limited agent ACROSS THE POPULATION with each persona's own search depth and slip rate, and the gate is on the MEDIAN persona rather than the mean or the best. The 8,000-conversation trait pool is what makes this a measurement rather than an assumption about who plays.

REVISION 9 - THE LYAPUNOV REMEDY IS ORDERED IN ADVANCE.

The finding: "Shorter Horizons is the least costly. It preserves the physics and the momentum while limiting the window of predictability. Damping is the most expensive as it violates the momentum requirement."

Adopted verbatim as a pre-registered remedy order, so it is not chosen after seeing which one flatters the result: shorten the horizon first, reduce body count second, add damping LAST and only with the finding recorded -- because damping is in direct conflict with revision 5, which requires the system to have momentum of its own. A game that passes N3 only by damping the dynamics into stillness has passed by becoming game two on a prettier board.

REVISION 10 - STRATEGY CLASSES ARE DISTINGUISHED TOPOLOGICALLY.

The finding: "A strategy class is defined by the manifold of the intervention vector. If a change in intervention type results in a non-continuous jump in the solution space, it is a new class. If it is a smooth gradient, it is the same class with different parameters."

So DIVERSITY stops counting labelled strategies -- which would have counted my own naming as evidence -- and tests for discontinuity: perturb the intervention vector continuously and look for a jump in outcome. Smooth means one class. That makes the diversity metric independent of what I decided to call things, which the counting version was not.

═══════════ REVISION 11 · WHAT TWO CHEMICAL RUNS TAUGHT, APPLIED HERE ═══════════

Game two has now been through two complete Monte Carlo cycles. The tally is the
reason this section exists: ACROSS BOTH RUNS, INSTRUMENT DEFECTS OUTNUMBERED
DESIGN FINDINGS ROUGHLY TWO TO ONE. Nine defects were in the measuring apparatus
and four were in the game. Every one of the nine would have produced a confident,
wrong number.

So the following are not refinements of the Darkmatter plan's content. They
change HOW THE RUN IS CONDUCTED, and each one is the scar of a specific failure.

(A) EVERY CONTROL MUST SEARCH FOR A LIVE CASE AND ASSERT NON-TRIVIALITY.

Four vacuous controls, all the same shape: a hardcoded seed or case that did not
exercise the thing being checked, so the check passed on equality.

    C6   compared a replay score of 0 to 0 on a seed that never scored
    N1   compared two identical banks because the agent never declared
    N1'  then compared two DIFFERENT BEHAVIOURS rather than one behaviour with
         and without the forfeit -- a confounded control that read backwards
    F6   a correlation of 1.000 from a series with no variance (game one)

RULE: a control scans for a case where the effect can actually occur, asserts
the effect is non-zero, and where it compares two configurations it holds the
ACTION LIST fixed so only the rule under test differs.

(B) NO METRIC BECOMES A GATE UNTIL ITS NULL MODEL IS MEASURED.

The seed-share bar of 35% was imported from Farkle, which scores in thousands,
into a game scoring 0-8 integers. A permutation null -- shuffle which seed each
result belongs to, destroying the seed effect while keeping every marginal --
showed a floor of 19.5% manufactured by discreteness alone. Roughly 20 of the 52
observed points were the ruler rather than the liquid.

Darkmatter's ATTRIBUTION, LYAPUNOV and DIVERSITY gates all have this hazard and
none of them has a null yet. Each gets one BEFORE it is compared to a threshold.

(C) THE CEILING MUST SHARE A VERB SET WITH THE AGENTS, CHECKED STRUCTURALLY.

Twice a "ceiling" scored below a bounded agent, because the beam could not use a
verb its agents had. An unbounded search can always play a bounded agent's move,
so a negative solver margin is arithmetic reporting a broken evaluator. In
Darkmatter the verbs are interventions and the hazard is identical.

(D) ANTI-NIM TRAVELS WITH EVERY CONSEQUENCE OR CONFLICT METRIC.

EFFECTIVE BRANCHING (moves within 10% of the best) and MOVE-VALUE ENTROPY are
added to Darkmatter's gates. Chemistry passed them comfortably -- 14.2 live moves
and 5.23 bits -- which is what established that its terrain is wide and its
horizon short. Without them a high-stakes, high-conflict, three-move game passes
everything.

(E) INFORMATION IS NOT A DEPTH LEVER, AND OBSERVABILITY IS THE SAME DIAL.

Order preview bought 31.6 points of agency floor by spending 47 points of solver
margin: the planner went from 63% to 88% of the ceiling. Showing the player more
converts unreachable ceiling into reachable skill; it does not create skill.

G7 OBSERVABILITY is exactly this dial wearing a different name. It must be
reported against solver margin, not against agency alone, or Darkmatter will
rediscover the same trade and call it a win.

(F) A MECHANIC THAT NARROWS THE STATE SPACE SHORTENS THE HORIZON.

The declared route was built on the premise that an unrecoverable sunk cost would
lengthen consequence. It is load-bearing -- never-declare reaches only 77% of it
-- and its horizon is LOWER exactly where it works, because narrowing what you
should do is what commitment MEANS. Your own reading: "a stabilizer that forces
the game toward a terminal state rather than an engine that expands the tree."

Darkmatter's G5 INTERVENTION verbs need screening for this. A verb that
constrains the system is a convergence engine and will look like depth in every
metric except the horizon.

(G) BUDGET IS MEASURED BEFORE THE DESIGN SIZE IS COMMITTED.

Run one timed three cells only AFTER committing to 64, found 4.6 hours against a
4-hour cap, and had to cut two factors mid-run. The cost per cell is measured
first now, and the design is sized to it.

(H) RENDER BEFORE MEASURING, NOT AFTER.

Four visual defects in game two's screen, and the deepest was a RULE interacting
with a readout: the display's brightest state was unreachable, because "the order
is on the board" is never true under anywhere-delivery. No amount of balancing
would have found it; one screenshot did.

A 3D or 4D universe has a far larger surface for that class of defect than a
grid. So Darkmatter renders a universe and looks at it BEFORE stage 1, not after
stage 5.

(I) WHAT A RUN IS ENTITLED TO CONCLUDE, WRITTEN BEFORE IT RUNS.

Negative selection is not positive selection. If Darkmatter's factors fail, the
claim is "these factors failed" and not "a physics sandbox cannot be a game".

questions.text: Nine instrument defects against four design findings across two runs. Is that ratio evidence my process is working (it caught them) or that my instruments are built too carelessly in the first place — and what would distinguish those two readings?
Revision E says observability is the same dial as order preview and must be reported against solver margin. Does that make G7 not worth screening at all, since we already know what it trades?

Revision F warns that an intervention verb which constrains the system is a convergence engine. For a physics sandbox, is there any intervention verb that EXPANDS the reachable state space rather than narrowing it?
Revision H moves rendering before stage 1. What is the risk of looking at a universe before it is balanced — does seeing it bias which factors I then choose to screen?
With all eleven revisions, is this plan now better than the one you approved at r3, or have I added ceremony that will slow the run without catching anything new?
